---
title: Manifest reference
description: Component metadata lives in the act:component custom section, merged at build time from language manifests and an optional act.toml patch.
---

import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`act-build pack` writes the `act:component` WASM custom section (CBOR-encoded). Its contents are **merged** from several sources:

1. **Base** — `name`, `version`, `description` from the language manifest (`Cargo.toml`,
   `pyproject.toml`, or `package.json`)
2. **Inline patch** — the ACT table inside that same manifest: `[package.metadata.act]` (Rust),
   `[tool.act]` (Python), or `"act"` (JS/TS)
3. **`act.toml`** — sidecar patch, applied last and therefore highest priority
4. `act-build pack --set <key>=<value>` — a final per-invocation override

Later sources override earlier ones (RFC 7396 merge-patch). Note that the SDK macros contribute
*tool* definitions at compile time, not component metadata: `pack` resolves the manifest from
these files and writes the `act:component` section from them.

## Basic fields

Keys live under `[std]`. Name, version, and description come from the language manifest by default.

<Tabs syncKey="lang">
<TabItem label="Rust">
```toml
# Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "component-sqlite"
version = "0.2.3"
description = "SQLite database"

[package.metadata.act]
# optional overrides/additions
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Python">
```toml
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "python-eval"
version = "0.1.1"
description = "Python interpreter"

[tool.act.std]
# optional overrides/additions
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="act.toml">
```toml
[std]
name = "sqlite"               # last-wins override of the Cargo / pyproject name
version = "0.2.3"
description = "SQLite database"
```
</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Capability declarations

A component declares the WASI capabilities it needs. The host uses this as a **ceiling** on what the user's policy can grant: an undeclared capability, or a declaration with an empty `allow` list, is a hard deny regardless of what the operator grants.

### Filesystem

```toml
[std.capabilities."wasi:filesystem"]
description = "Stores the database file."

[[std.capabilities."wasi:filesystem".allow]]
path = "**"        # glob; "**" means any path
mode = "rw"        # "ro" or "rw"
```

Multiple `[[...allow]]` entries are OR'd. The user's runtime policy is intersected with this ceiling.

### HTTP

```toml
[std.capabilities."wasi:http"]
description = "Fetches OpenAPI specs from public catalogs."

[[std.capabilities."wasi:http".allow]]
host = "petstore3.swagger.io"   # "*" = any host; "*.example.com" = suffix
scheme = "https"                # optional — any scheme if absent
methods = ["GET"]               # optional — any method if absent
ports = [443]                   # optional — standard port for the scheme
```

### Sockets

```toml
[std.capabilities."wasi:sockets"]
description = "Connects to the configured Postgres server."

[[std.capabilities."wasi:sockets".allow]]
host = "*"
ports = [5432]                  # required
protocols = ["tcp"]
```

### Filesystem topology

Beyond authorization, a filesystem declaration can bind a host directory to a stable guest path,
so the component's code opens a fixed path regardless of who runs it. Authorization still comes
from the `allow` entries — keep the host paths in sync:

```toml
[[std.capabilities."wasi:filesystem".params.mounts]]
type = "bind"
guest = "/data"
host = "~/.my-component"
```

### Credentials

A component can declare the credentials it expects, which is what `act login` prompts for:

```toml
# Bare table — the class carries no constraints, but an undeclared class is
# denied outright, so this line is required to reach the credential store.
[std.capabilities."act:credentials"]

[[std.credentials]]
key = "default"                 # the key a session uses when its args name none
description = "iikoServer API user"

[[std.credentials.fields]]
key = "iiko-server:login"
label = "iikoServer login"

[[std.credentials.fields]]
key = "iiko-server:password"
label = "iikoServer password"
```

`act-build pack` refuses a manifest that declares `[[std.credentials]]` without the
`act:credentials` capability.

## Agent skill embedding

If a `skill/` directory exists at the package root, `act-build pack` tars it and embeds it as the `act:skill` custom section. Extract with `act skill <component.wasm> -o out/`. See [Agent Skills](/docs/build/skills/).

## Validation

```bash
act-build validate path/to/component.wasm
```

Checks that declared capabilities parse, that the CBOR section is readable, and that the file is a valid component.

## Merge order cheatsheet

```
┌───────────────────────────────┐
│ Cargo / pyproject / package   │  name, version, description
└───────────────────────────────┘
                ▼
┌───────────────────────────────┐
│ [package.metadata.act]        │  inline ACT table in that same manifest
│ [tool.act] / "act"            │
└───────────────────────────────┘
                ▼
┌───────────────────────────────┐
│ act.toml (sidecar)            │  the conventional home for capabilities
└───────────────────────────────┘
                ▼
┌───────────────────────────────┐
│ act-build pack --set k=v      │  per-invocation override (strings only)
└───────────────────────────────┘
                ▼
        act:component (CBOR)
```
